question.worked_solution:
First, we express $f$ as the composite function

$$
f=\operatorname{ln}⁡u,\,u=2\operatorname{sin}⁡v,\,v={e}^{x}.
$$

Differentiating gives

$$
\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}=\frac{1}{u},\,\frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}v}=2\operatorname{cos}⁡v,\,\frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x}={e}^{x}.
$$

Applying now the chain rule twice, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}x} & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{\text{d}f}{\text{d}u}\cdot \frac{\text{d}u}{\text{d}v}\cdot \frac{\text{d}v}{\text{d}x} \\  & =\frac{1}{u}\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡v)\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{1}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡{e}^{x}}\cdot (2\operatorname{cos}⁡({e}^{x}))\cdot {e}^{x} \\  & =\frac{2{e}^{x}\operatorname{cos}⁡({e}^{x})}{2\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{x})} \\  & ={e}^{x}\frac{\operatorname{cos}⁡({e}^{x})}{\operatorname{sin}⁡({e}^{x})} \\  & ={e}^{x}\operatorname{cot}⁡({e}^{x})\end{aligned}
$$
